# Rental market {#sec-rental}

## Median rent has climbed fastest since 2019, in every locality


::: {.cell layout-align="left"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Median rent has climbed fastest since 2019, in every locality](rental_files/figure-html/fig-median-rent-1.png){#fig-median-rent fig-align='left' fig-alt='Grouped horizontal bar chart of median gross rent for eight Richmond-area localities and Virginia in 2014, 2019, and 2024, in nominal dollars. The 2014 bars are muted grey. Every locality\'s 2024 bar is well above its 2019 bar. New Kent has the highest 2024 median rent at $1,721, up 70 percent since 2019 alone, the sharpest increase in the region. Charles City has the lowest 2024 median rent at $1,099.' width=100%}
:::
:::


- **Every locality posted a higher median gross rent in 2024 than in 2019, and in all eight the 2019-to-2024 increase outpaced the full 2014-to-2019 span.**
- New Kent had the region's highest 2024 median rent at $1,721, up 70 percent since 2019 alone — the sharpest increase in the region.
- Richmond city's median rent rose 34 percent since 2019, from $1,025 to $1,372 — yet stayed below the statewide median of $1,579.
- Powhatan had the slowest rent growth since 2019, at 19 percent; small-county medians (New Kent, Powhatan, Goochland, Charles City) carry wide margins of error and describe small renter stocks.
- All figures are nominal dollars; inflation-adjusted comparisons come with the cost-burden analysis.

## Renter shares held steady since 2019, except in the smallest counties


::: {.cell layout-align="left"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Renter shares held steady since 2019, except in the smallest counties](rental_files/figure-html/fig-renter-share-1.png){#fig-renter-share fig-align='left' fig-alt='Dumbbell chart comparing the renter share of households in 2019 and 2024 for eight Richmond-area localities and Virginia. Richmond city has by far the highest renter share, near 57 percent in both years. Henrico is near 36 percent in both years, and Virginia near 33 percent. The six remaining counties are all below 25 percent, and the smallest counties are lowest in 2024: New Kent and Powhatan each fell to about 7 percent.' width=100%}
:::
:::


- **The region added roughly 10,656 renter households between 2019 and 2024, a 8% increase — faster growth than the full prior five years.**
- Richmond city drove the gain, adding about 7,107 renter households since 2019 — roughly NA of the regional increase — though its renter share held near 56% because total households grew just as fast.
- Chesterfield and Hanover renter counts grew steadily since 2019, but both counties remain more than three-quarters owner-occupied.
- The three smallest counties — Charles City, New Kent, and Powhatan — each lost renter households since 2019, deepening the ownership tilt of the outer region; New Kent's renter count fell 37 percent.
- Over the full decade, the region added 20,309 renter households (15%) — most of that growth came in the last five years.

## Asking rents are up 28 percent since 2020, even as the market has loosened


::: {.cell layout-align="left"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Asking rents are up 28 percent since 2020, even as the market has loosened](rental_files/figure-html/fig-costar-rent-1.png){#fig-costar-rent fig-align='left' fig-alt='Line chart of the average multifamily asking rent per unit in the eight-locality Richmond region, quarterly from 2020 through mid-2026, in nominal dollars, with a shaded band marking 2022 onward. The line rises from about $1,235 in early 2020 to $1,422 by early 2022 — the market\'s tightest point, with vacancy near 5.6 percent — then keeps climbing to $1,583 by the second quarter of 2026, even as vacancy rises to 8.5 percent.' width=100%}
:::
:::


- **Regional average asking rent reached $1,583 in 2026 Q2, up 28% from $1,235 in early 2020.**
- The market was tightest in early 2022 — vacancy near 6%, the low point of the period — and rents have risen another 11% since then, to $1,583.
- Vacancy has since climbed to 8.5% in 2026 Q2, above where it stood at the start of 2020, as new deliveries caught up with and then outpaced demand.
- CoStar coverage is professionally managed multifamily; New Kent and Charles City have only a handful of tracked properties, so locality-level trends there are not meaningful.

::: {.callout-note}
## Since 2022
The 2022 Framework flagged a regional average asking rent of $1,395 in early 2022 as a two-decade high with vacancy near 5%. Rents have since risen another 11% to $1,583, but the market has loosened: vacancy is now 8.5%, and rent growth has slowed sharply. The 2022 Framework also reported a net *loss* of renter households from 2016 to 2020 (with a COVID-era data caveat); the 2020–2024 ACS instead shows renter households growing across the region.
:::
